title: HTTP, REST & API Engineering
outcome: Design HTTP APIs using resources, methods, status codes, idempotency, errors, caching semantics, and versionable contracts.
artifact: A written TaskFlow API contract for tasks with request/response examples and deliberate error semantics.
labSteps: Write the task resource shape before writing controller code.
Design collection and item URIs and justify GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE choices.
Define success and failure status codes for create, read, update, delete, validation, auth, forbidden, and missing-resource cases.
Use curl or an API client to inspect raw headers and bodies rather than only frontend behavior.
Repeat safe/idempotent requests and reason about what should or should not change.
Write an error envelope that the frontend can parse consistently.
failureModes: Encoding actions into routes when resource semantics are clearer
Returning database rows as accidental public contracts
Confusing authentication failures with authorization failures
mastery: Can design a resource-oriented route set
Can reason about API contract evolution
principles: Design APIs around resources, contracts, and HTTP semantics rather than controller method names.
Use status codes consistently so clients can distinguish validation, authentication, authorization, and missing resources.
Make request and response contracts explicit enough that frontend and backend can evolve safely.
Treat idempotency, pagination, errors, and concurrency as API design concerns, not afterthoughts.
